The Bahi is a traditional Assamese transverse flute made entirely from bamboo, played by blowing air across a side blow hole while controlling pitch through finger holes along the tube. It is one of the oldest melodic instruments in Assamese folk music and is prominently used during Rongali Bihu celebrations. Unlike the rhythm-keeping instruments of the Bihu ensemble, the Bahi carries the melodic layer with its soft, flute-like tone. It is traditionally played by men and is closely associated with pastoral and folk music traditions of Assam.

The Khuti-Taal is a small paired cymbal instrument made of bell metal, a brass alloy traditionally crafted in the Brahmaputra valley of Assam. It consists of two small metal discs connected by a cord and struck together to produce a bright, high-pitched ringing sound that provides rhythmic accompaniment during Bihu performances. The Khuti-Taal is traditionally played by both men and women and is commonly used alongside the Dhol and Pepa during Rongali Bihu performances. Its metallic timbre and compact size make it an important rhythm-keeping instrument in Assamese folk music.
